# Starter: Course / Class / Section modeling (round 2)

This is a small, self-contained TypeScript project (its own `package.json`,
not part of the Berkeleytime monorepo) with an in-memory implementation of
Berkeleytime's REAL Course/Class/Section/Enrollment model -- see
`src/types.ts` for the entities and how they relate, and `src/data.ts` for
the fixture data.

If you did round 1 of this exercise, compare your own design against this
one. They will not match exactly, and that's fine -- see the note at the
bottom of this file about what to write up.

## Setup

```
npm install
npm test        # runs the test suite once
npm run test:watch
```

Both `src/scheduleConflict.ts` and `src/offeringHistory.ts` currently
`throw new Error("not implemented")`. Every test in `test/` is currently
failing. Your job is to implement both functions so the full suite passes.

## Task 1: schedule conflict detection

File: `src/scheduleConflict.ts`, function `findScheduleConflicts`.

Given the sections a student is already enrolled in and a candidate section
they're considering adding, return every enrolled section that has a
meeting-time conflict with the candidate (empty array if none).

- A conflict requires shared day(s) of the week AND overlapping
  `[startMinutes, endMinutes)` ranges.
- Back-to-back meetings (one ends exactly when the other starts) are NOT a
  conflict.
- A section can have more than one meeting entry (e.g. a lab meeting twice
  a week at different times) -- check all of them.

Full rules and edge cases are documented in the function's JSDoc in
`src/scheduleConflict.ts`. The fixtures exercising this function are in
`scheduleConflictSections` in `src/data.ts`; read the comment above that
object before you start -- it tells you exactly which sections are meant to
conflict and why.

## Task 2: cross-term course offering history

File: `src/offeringHistory.ts`, function `getCourseOfferingHistory`.

Given a courseId, return every Class ever offered for that course, across
every term, oldest to newest -- including offerings from before a
renumbering, and including every independent lecture sequence in a term
that had more than one. Terms with zero classes simply don't appear.

Full rules are documented in the function's JSDoc in
`src/offeringHistory.ts`. The fixtures are in `src/data.ts` -- in
particular `crs-econ1`, which was renumbered from "ECON 1" to "ECON 101A"
partway through its history, and `crs-ling142`, which has never had a
single class.

## What "done" looks like

`npm test` passes, with no changes to the `test/` directory or to the
fixtures in `src/data.ts`. Don't special-case fixture values inside the
implementation (e.g. `if (courseId === "crs-econ1")`) -- the grading pass
uses the same functions against a different fixture set.

## Write-up

In your submission, briefly note:

1. Where your round-1 design (if you did one) differed from this model,
   and why -- e.g. did you have Course and Class as one entity? Did you
   put enrollment counts on the Class instead of the Section? Was your
   join key for offering history something other than a stable `courseId`?
2. Any AI tool you used (which tool, and roughly what you asked it) --
   paste or summarize the prompts you used, not just "I used Copilot."
   We care about how you used it (did you have it draft the whole
   function and then check its edge-case handling yourself, or did you
   reason through the day/time-overlap logic first and use it to fill in
   boilerplate?), not whether you used it at all.
